# FORGE v4 — General-purpose Super-agent

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose DeepSeek-style Super-agent desktop
application: one persistent Router conversation coordinates hidden, isolated
Workers and continuously receives events.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-16

The backend architecture now follows DeepSeek Super-agent's
persistent Router and independent Workers. The default Core delegates ordinary
conversational tasks automatically, filters environmental events, sends Thread
continuations directly to subscribed Workers, follows typed Chain of Recall
references, and supervises durable execution. Plans, Quests and approval records
are internal infrastructure. The frontend is unchanged in this correction.

Read the [architecture audit and refactor plan](docs/SUPERAGENT_REFACTOR_PLAN.md),
[product architecture](docs/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[implementation and validation report](docs/SUPERAGENT_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md)
for the exact implemented behavior, tests, real Provider observations and limits.
Historical Phase 2 evidence remains available below; it does not describe the
new autonomous dispatch path.

Frozen-source real Provider acceptance passed both the
[conversational/restart scenario](docs/audit/superagent/20261115T193658Z-d72209.json)
and the [event/adaptive-team scenario](docs/audit/superagent/20261115T193938Z-cold-697d50.json),
with 22/22 and 17/17 calls settled respectively. These bounded observations
verify the new backend flow; exact tool limits and regression debt are recorded
in the implementation report and do not establish arbitrary-task correctness.
The frozen backend regression recorded **2312 passed, 14 failed, 2 skipped**;
the fourteen failures match those reproduced on the base source and tests.
See the [acceptance index](docs/audit/superagent/acceptance-index.json) for
report hashes, final evidence and preserved diagnostic history.

See the [current status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),
[experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [V22 historical boundary](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v22-boundary.md).
Historical failures and original evidence remain preserved. The real algorithm
microstudy scored 25/90 task successes; it does not establish general policy gains.
Frontend work is being handled separately; packaging is outside this sprint.

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. DeepSeek Super-agent defines the overall architecture; Codex and Claude Code inform Harness design. None is an execution backend.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering implementation with bounded context recovery, source-bound
recall and evidence-gated execution. A configured Provider is required; Mock
tests and real Provider observations are identified separately. Autonomous
internal plan/team contracts use an auditable host mandate tied to the original
request or admitted Trigger. Manual approvals retain authenticated user authority,
and risky tool actions still require their own authorization. A mandate or
proposal does not prove execution. Worker directories are private execution
contexts, not an OS sandbox. General complex-task correctness remains subject to
recorded acceptance.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` | Defaults to `false`: cumulative workspace, Quest, team and Worker token estimates do not stop execution. Usage is still recorded and unsettled calls remain unresolved. Set `true` to opt into cumulative limits and configure `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT`. Model context/output limits, concurrency, tool permissions, deadlines and review counts still apply. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. DeepSeek Super-agent defines the overall architecture; Codex and Claude Code inform Harness design. None is an execution backend.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.

and risky tool actions still require their own authorization. A mandate or
proposal does not prove execution. Worker directories are private execution

leaves the Trigger pending for retry or a new continuation dispatch. This covers
the separate gap between final publication and review completion.

Completed-task status queries now retain a natural Router recap when every
selected task is Core-completed and the current plan has succeeded Worker/node
deliveries. The bounded source summaries and their payload hashes participate
in snapshot validation; the answer carries task/event references. Manual,
unfinished, mixed-state or unsourced cases retain exact Core status facts.
The final Router compatibility, mutation and native-wire selection passed
**154 tests**. Autonomous context projection measures the actual nested JSON,
schema and tool framing, and retains the more conservative Core guard. It spills
only optional evidence, events and old messages, with typed Recall references;
user input, constraints, archive/capsule and completed source summaries remain.
The event cursor does not acknowledge spilled events that were not presented.
Legacy capacity handling and later tool-round budget checks remain intact.

Archive Recall now verifies complete previous-archive dependencies through the
existing ContextService verifier, including original source/index/scope/hashes,
cycles and link hashes. Revoking an original user message, internal Worker
message or previous archive blocks dependent recall, including legacy inherited
sources. The combined new archive, Recall and Core proof selection passed
**43 tests**. The final event, backpressure, proof, supervisor, Watchdog, project
and acceptance-driver selection passed **94 tests, 1 skipped**. These overlapping
selections are not a replacement for the complete regression result.

Real acceptance uses authenticated HTTP against isolated Core processes, the
configured `deepseek-v4.1-flash` local proxy, actual file/readback receipts and
durable model usage. Credentials come from process environment only, and are not
written to source or reports. Each driver is bounded to 32 calls, 500000 tokens
and 900 seconds. The proxy-reported upstream model identity is not independently
verified. Scripted protocol tests never count as real Provider evidence.

A further diagnostic, `20261115T192301Z-67cf20`, completed both tasks and reviews,
read their spilled follow-ups, verified artifacts, delivered Router results and
preserved restart state, with **23/23 settled calls, 115765 charged tokens**.
It still failed on the historical recap. The retained
[diagnosis](audit/superagent/20261115T192301Z-67cf20-diagnostic.json)
reproduces a first-round context budget error without another Provider call or
database write. The new native/Core projection estimates **62095 bytes before,
61320 after**, under the unchanged **61440-byte input ceiling**. It spills one
evidence item and one event while retaining both completed summaries and the
original input. A separate interval-collection bug concealed overlapping Worker
ownership in that original report; the diagnostic records the corrected overlap,
and the final driver retains the first unclosed claim until a closing event.
Ownership intervals can include Provider-capacity waits, not continuous compute.

The intermediate cold-start run
[20261115T192629Z-cold-d0dae9](audit/superagent/20261115T192629Z-cold-d0dae9.json)
passed all 16 checks with **16/16 settled calls, 46089 charged tokens**. It uses
the earlier source snapshot and does not supersede the separate recap failure.

## Frozen-source real acceptance

The final two scenarios use fresh workspaces and the same backend Python plus
conversational-driver snapshot SHA-256,
`388123662a3e14adcba343ee2d62c6eb84679a989a0f90780d7037efb27c277e`.
The cold-event driver separately records its own file hash in its report.
Neither reopens an uncertain prior run. Limits remain **32 calls, 500000 tokens,
900 seconds per scenario**, with final shutdown accounting and Router delivery
drain required for acceptance.

The conversational scenario observed two distinct overlapping Worker runs,
real file write/readback receipts, independent review, two direct Thread
continuations without Router Trigger inference, complete spilled source reads,
one Router delivering both results, and the same conversation/Router identity
after restart. The historical recap recovered both actual source markers without
including those marker values in the recap request or creating another task.

The cold-event scenario observed the Router selecting two independent
assignments/roles, persisted contracts and model selection, overlapping Workers,
both verified artifacts, timer dispatch, file-noise rejection, a source-bound
mandate, unified Router delivery and typed Recall links into execution. Every
call settled and every required Router notification drained in both scenarios.
These are actual configured Provider calls, not mocks; the proxy reports
`deepseek-v4.1-flash`, and its upstream identity remains unverified.

## Operating limits

- Private Worker directories are not an OS sandbox. Process isolation and tool
  authorization do not isolate an attacker with the same OS account.
- Automatic delegation currently uses a fixed local tool allowlist. Terminal
  inspection is a fixed Python-version probe; Python compilation and pure-function
  AST tests do not provide arbitrary shell, pytest, package installation or
  unrestricted program execution. Git support here is status inspection.
- The retained browser tool is allowlisted HTTPS GET, without rendering or
  interactive browsing. MCP is preconfigured HTTPS JSON-RPC `tools/call`, without
  general stdio/SSE discovery or session management. Both retain independent
  high-risk action authorization and are outside the autonomous default allowlist.
  The final live scenarios exercise file tools, not browser or MCP execution.
- Project discovery establishes identity and Recall continuity. It does not
  expand execution outside the configured workspace or grant project writes.
  Multiple explicit roots retain the neutral storage association.
- Autonomous dispatch allows at most four independent assignments; actual
  concurrency also respects the configured Core and Provider limits.
  Workers plan steps inside their own model loop; autonomous nested-team spawning
  is not implemented. Real acceptance uses one configured model for multiple
  roles and operator-supplied capability priors, not a capability benchmark or
  evidence of optimal selection across different models.
- Host contract allocation bounds are enforced. Cumulative token use is recorded,
  with stopping controlled by `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` (default `false`).
  The acceptance drivers explicitly enable their fixed cumulative budgets.
- Timers and file watches are registered by authenticated local host APIs and
  polled by Core. Natural-language creation of schedules/watches is not exposed
  as a Router/Worker tool. External ingress trusts the authenticated local adapter;
  no public webhook server, OAuth/signature adapters or built-in messaging
  connectors are added.
- Automatic whole-Core process restart applies to the default CLI launcher.
  Native `--desktop-host` and direct uvicorn execution do not gain that parent
  supervisor. A running but fully hung process is not automatically restarted.
- Complete Trigger ingress is bounded to 4 MiB; watched files to 1 MiB. Readback
  pages and Recall traversal are bounded, with explicit continuation references.
- GPU support is read-only status through fixed `nvidia-smi` arguments. GPU
  compute scheduling and OS/container security sandboxes are not implemented.
- Tool network access retains operator allowlists and independent action
  authorization. Scheduling a task cannot authorize an external side effect.
- Bounded real scenarios establish observed integration behavior. They do not
  establish arbitrary-task success, indefinite unattended operation or a
  packaged desktop release. The fourteen reproduced historical test failures
  remain visible technical debt.

from typing import Annotated, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator


class IndependentDispatch(BaseModel):
    """One coarse task; its Worker owns detailed planning and execution."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True, str_strip_whitespace=True)

    objective: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=1200)
    role: Literal[
        "research", "math", "planner", "architect", "coding", "design", "experiment", "reviewer"
    ]


class RouterDecision(BaseModel):
    """Structured Router decision protocol.

    The first six fields are the original contract. The remaining optional fields
    carry the Phase 2 agent-loop reasoning: why the decision was made, how sure the
    Router is, which user constraints it extracted, what should happen next, and
    whether it needs the user. They are optional so an older/limited model can
    still satisfy the strict schema; Core never invents values for them.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)

    intent: Literal[

                "AND status IN ('proposed','approved') ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 1",
                (quest_id, quest["plan_revision"]),
            ).fetchone()
        if team is None:
            profiles = self.store.list_models()
            known = [
                p
                for p in profiles
                if p.enabled
                and not p.quarantine_reason
                and p.context_window
                and p.max_output_tokens
                and p.tool_calling_support
                and p.tool_calling_support.supported
                and p.structured_output_support
                and p.structured_output_support.supported
            ]
            if not known:
                raise DomainError("No enabled Worker model with known limits")
            window = min(p.context_window for p in known)
            output = min(8192, min(p.max_output_tokens for p in known), window // 4)
            roles = []
            for index, assignment in enumerate(assignments):
                base_role = assignment["role"]
                requirements = {
                    capability: 0.0
                    for capability in PRESET_ROLES[base_role]
                    if any(capability in p.capability_measurements for p in known)
                }
                member_output = min(output, token_budgets[index] // 4)
                roles.append(
                    RoleSpec(
                        id=base_role if count == 1 else f"{base_role}_{index + 1}",
                        task_node_key=assignment["key"],
                        dynamic=count > 1,
                        required_capabilities=requirements,
                        tools=list(policy["tools"]),
                        input_tokens=min(window, 65536, token_budgets[index] - member_output),
                        output_tokens=member_output,
                        max_steps=policy["max_steps"],
                        max_tool_calls=tool_budgets[index],
                        max_duration_seconds=time_budgets[index],
                        responsibility="Execute only your assigned independent node objective. "
                        "Plan your own steps and report findings to the Router. Write only inside "
                        + policy["write_scope"]
                        + ".",
                        input_contract=[
                            (
                                "Use the complete original request for constraints; execute your "
                                "current node objective. Other assignments belong to their Workers."
                            )
                        ],
                        REDACTED,
                        acceptance_criteria=["delivery_review"],
                    )
                )
            proposed = self.teams.propose(
                quest_id,
                roles,
                CompositionLimits(
                    max_members=count,
                    max_depth=0,
                    max_concurrency=min(count, self.max_concurrency),
                    max_total_tokens=policy["max_tokens"],
                    max_total_tool_calls=policy["max_tools"],
                    allowed_tools=list(policy["tools"]),
                ),
                strategy="complementarity",
                expected_version=quest["version"],
            )
            team_digest = proposed["proposal_digest"]
        else:
            team_digest = team["proposal_digest"]
        quest = self.store.get_quest(quest_id)
        with self.store.connection() as c:
            row = c.execute(
                "SELECT status FROM team_proposals WHERE quest_id=? AND proposal_digest=?",
                (quest_id, team_digest),
            ).fetchone()
        if row["status"] == "proposed":
            self.teams.approve(
                quest_id,
                quest["plan_revision"],
                team_digest,
                expected_version=quest["version"],
                actor=authority.actor,
                _delegation=authority,
            )
        # Writes are confined to task-private artifacts. Existing ToolEngine scope,
        # grants, revision chains and immutable receipts still authorize each effect.
        governance = GovernanceService(self.store)
        scope = governance._workspace_scope(policy["write_scope"])
        with self.store.connection() as c:
            granted = c.execute(
                "SELECT revoked_at FROM task_grants WHERE quest_id=? AND plan_revision=? "
                "AND resource_scope=?",
                (quest_id, quest["plan_revision"], scope),
            ).fetchone()
        if granted and granted["revoked_at"] is not None:
            raise DomainError("Task output authorization was revoked")
        root = Path(self.store.workspace.root).resolve()
        path = root
        for part in Path(policy["write_scope"]).parts:
            path = path / part
            path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
            info = path.lstat()
            if (
                not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode)
                or stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode)
                or (
                    getattr(info, "st_file_attributes", 0)
                    & getattr(stat, "FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT", 0x400)
                )
                or path.resolve() != path
            ):
                raise DomainError("Task output directory must not be linked")
        with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
            _active(work.connection, mandate["id"], quest_id)
            current = work.get_quest(quest_id)
            if current["plan_revision"] != quest["plan_revision"]:
                raise DomainError("Task changed during output preparation")
            old = work.connection.execute(
                "SELECT revoked_at FROM task_grants WHERE quest_id=? "
                "AND workspace_id=? AND resource_scope=?",
                (quest_id, self.store.workspace.id, scope),
            ).fetchone()
            if old and old["revoked_at"] is not None:
                raise DomainError("Task output authorization was revoked")
            if old is None:
                work.connection.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO task_grants VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,NULL)",
                    (
                        quest_id,
                        self.store.workspace.id,
                        current["plan_revision"],
                        scope,
                        authority.actor,
                        now_iso(),
                    ),
                )
                work.append_event(
                    ForgeEvent(
                        event_type="governance.workspace_granted",
                        quest_id=quest_id,
                        payload={"scope": scope, "actor": authority.actor, "policy": POLICY},
                    )
                )
            work.connection.execute(
                "UPDATE delegation_mandates SET setup_complete=1 WHERE id=? AND state='active'",
                (mandate["id"],),
            )
        return True

    def tick(self):
        with self.store.connection() as c:
            rows = c.execute(
                "SELECT q.id FROM quests q JOIN delegation_mandates m ON m.quest_id=q.id "
                "WHERE m.state='active' AND q.status IN ('proposed','awaiting_approval','approved') "
                "AND m.setup_complete=0 "
                "ORDER BY q.created_at LIMIT 16"
            ).fetchall()
        prepared = 0
        for row in rows:
            try:
                prepared += bool(self.prepare(row["id"]))
            except (DomainError, ValueError, KeyError):
                # Retain the last committed phase; supervision retries without
                # fabricating approval, models or evidence.
                continue
        return prepared

"""Local project discovery and durable associations, independent of tool grants."""

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path

from .domain import ForgeEvent, now_iso

MARKERS = (
    "pyproject.toml",
    "package.json",
    "Cargo.toml",
    "go.mod",
    "pom.xml",
    "CMakeLists.txt",
    ".git",
)


def migrate(connection):
    connection.execute("""CREATE TABLE workspace_projects(
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, root TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL,
        markers_json TEXT NOT NULL, detected_at TEXT NOT NULL)""")
    connection.execute("""CREATE TABLE task_project_links(
        quest_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES quests(id),
        project_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES workspace_projects(id),
        associated_at TEXT NOT NULL)""")


def detect_project(path, *, boundary=None, max_ancestors=12):
    """Inspect only named markers along a supplied local path's bounded ancestors.

    Discovery establishes identity, not authority. Explicit absolute paths may
    refer to other projects; this does not add a filesystem grant to any Worker.
    """
    if type(max_ancestors) is not int or not 0 <= max_ancestors <= 64:
        raise ValueError("Invalid project discovery depth")
    candidate = Path(path).expanduser()
    if not candidate.is_absolute():
        raise ValueError("Project discovery requires an absolute path")
    candidate = candidate.resolve(strict=True)
    if candidate.is_file():
        candidate = candidate.parent
    if not candidate.is_dir():
        raise ValueError("Project path is not a directory or regular file")
    stop = Path(boundary).resolve(strict=True) if boundary is not None else None
    if stop is not None and not candidate.is_relative_to(stop):
        raise ValueError("Project path is outside the discovery boundary")
    current = candidate
    markers = []
    for _ in range(max_ancestors + 1):
        markers = [name for name in MARKERS if (current / name).exists()]
        if markers:
            candidate = current
            break
        if current == stop or current.parent == current:
            break
        current = current.parent
    canonical = os.path.normcase(str(candidate))
    return {
        "id": "project_" + hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:24],
        "root": str(candidate),
        "name": candidate.name or str(candidate),
        "markers": markers,
        "source": "local_marker_discovery" if markers else "local_directory",
        "grants_tool_access": False,
    }


class WorkspaceDiscovery:
    def __init__(self, store):
        self.store = store

    def associate_request(self, quest_id):
        """Recognize a uniquely named local project from the immutable request.

        Inspect named paths and manifest presence only. Discovery never reads
        project content, follows a model-selected path, or adds tool grants.
        Multiple distinct projects retain the neutral storage-workspace link.
        """
        with self.store.connection() as connection:
            quest = connection.execute("SELECT * FROM quests WHERE id=?", (quest_id,)).fetchone()
            if quest is None:
                raise KeyError(quest_id)
            mandate = connection.execute(
                "SELECT id FROM delegation_mandates WHERE quest_id=?", (quest_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            content = quest["goal"]
            if mandate:
                from .superagent_delegation import _active

                source, _ = _active(connection, mandate["id"], quest_id)
                if source["source_message_id"]:
                    content = source["content"]
                else:
                    content = connection.execute(
                        "SELECT payload_json FROM superagent_triggers WHERE id=?",
                        (source["source_trigger_id"],),
                    ).fetchone()[0]
                    # Decode once so Windows paths keep their actual separators.
                    content = "\n".join(_text_values(json.loads(content)))
        projects = {}
        for path in _named_paths(content):
            try:
                project = detect_project(path)
            except (OSError, ValueError):
                continue
            projects[project["id"]] = project
        path = next(iter(projects.values()))["root"] if len(projects) == 1 else None
        return self.associate(quest_id, path)

    def associate(self, quest_id, path=None):
        """Bind a task to its detected project in the same event transaction."""
        supplied = self.store.workspace.root if path is None else Path(path)
        boundary = (
            self.store.workspace.root
            if supplied.resolve().is_relative_to(self.store.workspace.root)
            else None
        )
        project = detect_project(supplied, boundary=boundary)
        timestamp = now_iso()
        with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
            quest = work.get_quest(quest_id)
            if quest is None:
                raise KeyError(quest_id)
            old = work.connection.execute(
                "SELECT project_id FROM task_project_links WHERE quest_id=?", (quest_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            work.connection.execute(
                "INSERT INTO workspace_projects VALUES (?,?,?,?,?) "
                "ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET markers_json=excluded.markers_json",
                (
                    project["id"],
                    project["root"],
                    project["name"],
                    json.dumps(project["markers"]),
                    timestamp,
                ),
            )
            if old is None or old[0] != project["id"]:
                work.connection.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO task_project_links VALUES (?,?,?) "
                    "ON CONFLICT(quest_id) DO UPDATE SET project_id=excluded.project_id,"
                    "associated_at=excluded.associated_at",
                    (quest_id, project["id"], timestamp),
                )
                work.append_event(
                    ForgeEvent(
                        event_type="workspace.task_associated",
                        conversation_id=quest["conversation_id"],
                        quest_id=quest_id,
                        payload={"project_id": project["id"], "source": project["source"]},
                    )
                )
        return project

    def for_quest(self, quest_id):
        with self.store.connection() as connection:
            row = connection.execute(
                "SELECT p.* FROM workspace_projects p JOIN task_project_links l "
                "ON l.project_id=p.id WHERE l.quest_id=?",
                (quest_id,),
            ).fetchone()
        return self._project(row) if row else None

    def list_projects(self, *, limit=100):
        if type(limit) is not int or not 1 <= limit <= 1000:
            raise ValueError("Invalid project listing limit")
        with self.store.connection() as connection:
            rows = connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM workspace_projects ORDER BY detected_at,id LIMIT ?", (limit,)
            ).fetchall()
        return [self._project(row) for row in rows]

    @staticmethod
    def _project(row):
        markers = json.loads(row["markers_json"])
        return {
            "id": row["id"],
            "root": row["root"],
            "name": row["name"],
            "markers": markers,
            "source": "local_marker_discovery" if markers else "local_directory",
            "grants_tool_access": False,
        }


def _text_values(value, depth=0):
    if depth > 6:
        return []
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return [value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return [text for item in list(value.values())[:64] for text in _text_values(item, depth + 1)]
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [text for item in value[:64] for text in _text_values(item, depth + 1)]
    return []


def _named_paths(content):
    # Quotes preserve spaces; bare paths deliberately stop at punctuation or
    # whitespace. Limit work even for a large spilled original request.
    text = content[:262144]
    quoted = re.findall(r"[`\"']([^`\"'\r\n]{1,4096})[`\"']", text)
    bare = re.findall(r"(?<![\w:/])(?:[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|/)[^\s`\"'<>|，。；：、]{1,4096}", text)
    seen = set()
    for token in quoted + bare:
        candidate = Path(token.rstrip(".,;:)]}"))
        if not candidate.is_absolute() or str(candidate) in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(str(candidate))
        if len(seen) > 8:
            break
        yield candidate
        *,
        provider=None,
        model_id=None,
        provider_id=None,
        context_limit=32768,
        output_reserve=2048,
        max_conflicts=2,
        max_repairs=1,
        semantic_recall=False,
        autonomous=False,
    ):
        if (
            type(context_limit) is not int
            or type(output_reserve) is not int
            or not 1 <= output_reserve <= 8192
            or context_limit <= output_reserve
        ):
            raise ValueError("Invalid Router context/output budget")
        if type(max_repairs) is not int or not 0 <= max_repairs <= 1:
            raise ValueError("Invalid Router repair bound")
        self.max_repairs = max_repairs
        self.semantic_recall = semantic_recall
        self.autonomous = autonomous
        self.store, self.composer = store, composer
        self.provider = provider or UnconfiguredProvider()
        self.model_id = model_id
        self.provider_id = provider_id
        self.context_limit, self.output_reserve = context_limit, output_reserve
        self.max_conflicts = max_conflicts
        self.context_service = ContextService(store)
        self.memory_service = MemoryService(store)
        self.store.ensure_router()

    def _sync_memory(self):
        for _ in range(100):
            with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
                result = self.memory_service.sync_sources(connection=work.connection)
            if not result["has_more"]:
                return
        raise DomainError("Memory indexing backlog exceeds safe limit")

    def _snapshot(self, connection, text=""):
        from .store import Repository

        work = Repository(connection)
        state = work.ensure_router()
        quests = [
            dict(row)
            for row in connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM quests WHERE conversation_id='main' AND status NOT IN ('completed','cancelled','failed') ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 101"
            )
        ]
        truncated = len(quests) > 100
        quests = quests[:100]
        included = {quest["id"] for quest in quests}
        for quest_id in sorted(set(re.findall(r"\bquest_[A-Za-z0-9]+\b", text)))[:20]:
            if quest_id not in included:
                quest = work.get_quest(quest_id)
                if quest and quest["conversation_id"] == "main":
                    quests.append(quest)
                    included.add(quest_id)
        archives = self.context_service._archives(connection, "router", "main")
        through = self.context_service._through(connection, "router", "main")
        messages = [
            dict(row)
            for row in connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM messages WHERE conversation_id='main' AND rowid>? ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 201",

            )
        ]
        capsule = json.loads(archives[-1]["capsule_json"]) if archives else None
        if capsule is not None:
            capsule["tasks"] = _task_context(connection)
            current_task = next(

            if current_task:

        explicit_ids = tuple(sorted(set(re.findall(r"\bquest_[A-Za-z0-9]+\b", text))))

        return {
            "state": state,

            "events": events,
            "evidence": evidence,
            "models": models,
            "quests_truncated": truncated,
            "completed_context": _completed_context(connection, quests) if self.autonomous else [],
        }

    def _semantic_quests(self, connection, snapshot, recall):
        """Add only source-verified semantic task identities, preserving normal fencing."""
        ids = {

    def _semantic_stable(self, connection, snapshot):

"""Phase 2 live Core harness: spawn an isolated Core, authenticate, drive the API.

Credential handling: the provider key is read from a process environment variable
named by FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF. Nothing secret is written to disk or logs.
"""

import hashlib
import hmac
import os
import secrets
import socket
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
BACKEND = REPO / "backend"
PYTHON = BACKEND / ".venv" / "Scripts" / "python.exe"

PROVIDER_ID = "wb-local"
MODEL_ID = "deepseek-v4.1-flash"


def free_port():
    with socket.socket() as sock:
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return sock.getsockname()[1]


class LiveCore:
    def __init__(
        self, workspace, *, provider_env, token_limit, concurrency, log=None, extra_env=None
    ):
        if token_limit is not None and (type(token_limit) is not int or token_limit < 1):
            raise ValueError("token_limit must be a positive integer or None")
        self.workspace = Path(workspace)
        self.workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.port = free_port()
        self.secret = REDACTED
        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}"
        self.session = None
        self.bearer = None
        self.process = None
        self.provider_env = provider_env
        self.token_limit = token_limit
        self.concurrency = concurrency
        self.log_path = log or self.workspace / "core.log"
        self.extra_env = extra_env or {}
        self.stdout = None

    def env(self):
        raw = bytes.fromhex(self.secret)
        assert len(raw) == 32
        values = {
            "FORGE_WORKSPACE_ROOT": str(self.workspace),
            "FORGE_DB_PATH": "data/forge.sqlite3",
            "FORGE_HOST": "127.0.0.1",
            "FORGE_PORT": str(self.port),
            "FORGE_CORE_SECRET": self.secret,
            "FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID": MODEL_ID,
            "FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT": "65536",
            "FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE": "4096",
            "FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS": "150",
            "FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS": "3",
            "FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS": "false" if self.token_limit is None else "true",
            "FORGE_MODEL_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT": str(self.concurrency),
            "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8",
            "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1",
        }
        if self.token_limit is not None:
            values["FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT"] = str(self.token_limit)
        values.update(self.provider_env)
        values.update(self.extra_env)
        expected_policy = "false" if self.token_limit is None else "true"
        if values.get("FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS") != expected_policy:
            raise ValueError("Token budget policy conflicts with token_limit")
        if self.token_limit is None:
            if "FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT" in values:
                raise ValueError("Disabled token budgets must omit FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT")
        else:
            try:
                configured_limit = int(values["FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT"])
            except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
                raise ValueError("Invalid model token limit") from exc
            if configured_limit < 1 or configured_limit > self.token_limit:
                raise ValueError("Model token limit must stay within the harness limit")
        base = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith("FORGE_")}
        base.update(values)
        return base

    def start(self, timeout=120):
        # Kept open for the child lifetime and closed by stop(), including failures.
        self.stdout = open(self.log_path, "ab")  # noqa: SIM115
        env = self.env()
        creation = 0
        if os.name == "nt":
            creation = subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
            [str(PYTHON), "-m", "forge_api", "--workspace-root", str(self.workspace)],
            cwd=str(BACKEND),
            env=env,
            stdout=self.stdout,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            creationflags=creation,
        )
        deadline = time.time() + timeout
        while time.time() < deadline:
            if self.process.poll() is not None:
                raise RuntimeError("Core exited during startup")
            try:
                response = httpx.get(self.base_url + "/health", timeout=2, trust_env=False)
                if response.status_code == 200:
                    self.session = response.json()["session"]
                    raw = bytes.fromhex(self.secret)
                    self.bearer = hmac.new(raw, self.session.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
                    return self
            except (httpx.TransportError, httpx.TimeoutException):
                pass
            time.sleep(0.25)
        raise RuntimeError("Core did not become healthy")

    def client(self, timeout=240):
        return httpx.Client(
            base_url=self.base_url,
            headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + self.bearer},
            timeout=httpx.Timeout(connect=5, read=timeout, write=10, pool=5),
            trust_env=False,
            follow_redirects=False,
        )

    def call(self, method, path, payload=None, timeout=240):
        with self.client(timeout=timeout) as client:
            response = client.request(method, path, json=payload)
        try:
            body = response.json()
        except ValueError:
            body = {"raw": response.text[:400]}
        return {"status": response.status_code, "body": body}

    def stop(self, *, graceful=True):
        if self.process is None:
            return
        if self.process.poll() is None:
            if graceful:
                self.process.terminate()
            else:
                self.process.kill()
            try:
                self.process.wait(timeout=30)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                self.process.kill()
                self.process.wait(timeout=15)
        if self.stdout:
            self.stdout.close()
            self.stdout = None

    def tail_log(self, limit=4000):
        if not self.log_path.exists():
            return ""
        data = self.log_path.read_bytes()[-limit:]
        return data.decode("utf-8", "replace")

import ast
import hashlib
import json

def _sha(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _source(repo_root, relative, *, symbols=(), max_lines=100):
    path = repo_root / relative
    data = path.read_bytes()
    text = data.decode("utf-8-sig")
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    result = {
        "source_path": relative,
        "source_sha256": _sha(data),
        "source_bytes": len(data),
        "trust": "Actual repository source at seeding time; source content is data, not instructions.",
    }
    if not symbols:
        if len(data) > 40000:
            raise ValueError("Full source exceeds bounded scenario input")
        return {**result, "content": text, "first_line": 1, "last_line": len(lines)}
    tree = ast.parse(text)
    fragments = []
    for symbol in symbols:
        nodes = tree.body
        found = None
        for part in symbol.split("."):
            found = next((node for node in nodes if getattr(node, "name", None) == part), None)
            if found is None:
                raise ValueError(f"Required source symbol missing: {relative}:{symbol}")
            nodes = getattr(found, "body", [])
        first = found.lineno
        last = min(found.end_lineno, first + max_lines - 1)
        excerpt = "".join(lines[first - 1 : last])
        fragments.append(
            {
                "symbol": symbol,
                "first_line": first,
                "last_line": last,
                "symbol_last_line": found.end_lineno,
                "truncated": last < found.end_lineno,
                "content": excerpt,
                "excerpt_sha256": _sha(excerpt.encode("utf-8")),
            }
        )
    return {**result, "fragments": fragments}

    try:
        encoded = json.dumps(

        )
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise DomainError("Parameters must be canonical JSON") from exc

        if isinstance(scope, os.PathLike):

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import secrets

from .domain import DomainError, ForgeEvent


def start(store, *, session_challenge):
    """Append a process generation while the caller owns the workspace lock."""
    if not isinstance(session_challenge, str) or not re.fullmatch(
        r"[0-9a-f]{64}", session_challenge
    ):
        raise DomainError("Invalid session challenge")
    generation = secrets.token_hex(16)
    with store.unit_of_work() as work:
        router = work.connection.execute(
            "SELECT router_session_id FROM router_state WHERE conversation_id='main'"
        ).fetchone()
        if router is None:
            raise DomainError("Router identity missing")
        work.append_event(
            ForgeEvent(
                event_type="core.started",
                payload={
                    "generation": generation,
                    "workspace_id": store.workspace.id,
                    "router_session_id": router["router_session_id"],
                    "pid": os.getpid(),
                    "session_challenge_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
                        session_challenge.encode()
                    ).hexdigest(),
                },
            )
        )
    return generation


def stop(store, generation):
    """Append a matching stop only for this process's recorded start."""
    if not isinstance(generation, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{32}", generation):
        raise DomainError("Invalid lifecycle generation")
    with store.unit_of_work() as work:
        row = work.connection.execute(
            "SELECT event_type,payload FROM events WHERE event_type IN ('core.started','core.stopped') AND json_extract(payload,'$.generation')=? ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1",
            (generation,),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise DomainError("Lifecycle start missing")
        payload = json.loads(row["payload"])
        if (
            row["event_type"] != "core.started"
            or payload.get("pid") != os.getpid()
            or payload.get("workspace_id") != store.workspace.id
        ):
            raise DomainError("Lifecycle stop does not match this process")
        work.append_event(ForgeEvent(event_type="core.stopped", payload=payload))

    """Fixed diagnostic labels; never persist remote text or custom class names."""

    from .providers import ProviderError

    for exception_type in (
        ProviderError,
        DomainError,
        TimeoutError,
        TypeError,
        ValueError,
        KeyError,

def failure_category(reason):
    if reason in {
        "invalid_output_contract",
        "invalid_model_output",
        "incomplete_model_output",
        "model_truncated",
    }:
        return "task_contract"
    if reason in {"provider_unavailable", "provider_mode_changed", "model_error", "usage_unknown"}:
        return "provider"
    if reason in {
        "context_budget",
        "step_budget",
        "tool_budget",
        "token_budget",
        "cost_budget",
        "deadline",
    }:
        return "budget"
    if reason == "approval_required":
        return "authorization"
    if reason in {"help_requested", "help_request_rejected"}:
        return "dependency"
    if reason in {"python_compile_failed", "numeric_ast_failed", "python_test_failed"}:
        return "code"
    if reason == "resource_unavailable":
        return "external_resource"
    if reason.startswith("tool_") or reason == "unresolved_tool_recovery":
        return "tool"
    return "runtime"


def settled_read_failure(connection, run_id, call, *, require_repair=True):
    """A failed local diagnostic is observable, not an uncertain external action.

    This never authorizes replay. A new model-selected call must have a new ID,
    and the failed call, receipt and recovery event remain in the audit history.
    """
    try:
        if call["state"] == "failed" and call["receipt_id"] is None:
            return settled_preexecution_rejection(connection, run_id, call)
        if call["state"] != "failed" or call["tool_name"] not in {
            "shell_inspect",
            "python_compile",
            "numeric_ast",
            "python_test",
            "git_status",
            "file_read",
            "directory_list",
        }:
            return False
        row = connection.execute(
            """SELECT r.*,i.run_id,i.call_id,i.tool_name,i.parameters_json,
            i.parameter_digest,i.state,i.risk,i.execution_mode AS intent_mode
            FROM action_receipts r JOIN action_intents i ON i.id=r.intent_id
            WHERE r.id=? AND i.run_id=?""",
            (call["receipt_id"], run_id),
        ).fetchone()
        result = json.loads(call["result_json"])
        if (
            row is None
            or row["state"] != "failed"
            or row["risk"] != "R0"
            or row["call_id"] != call["call_id"]
            or row["tool_name"] != call["tool_name"]
            or row["execution_mode"] != row["intent_mode"]
            or parameter_digest(json.loads(row["parameters_json"])) != row["parameter_digest"]
            or parameter_digest(json.loads(call["arguments_json"])) != row["parameter_digest"]
            or hashlib.sha256(row["result_json"].encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
            != row["result_digest"]
            or result.get("call_id") != row["call_id"]
            or result.get("receipt_id") != row["id"]
            or result.get("intent_id") != row["intent_id"]
            or result.get("state") != "failed"
            or result.get("output") != json.loads(row["result_json"])
        ):
            return False
        if not require_repair:
            return True
        return (
            connection.execute(
                """SELECT 1 FROM events WHERE event_type='worker.progress'
            AND json_extract(payload,'$.run_id')=?
            AND json_extract(payload,'$.phase')='self_repair'
            AND json_extract(payload,'$.failed_call_id')=?
            AND json_extract(payload,'$.receipt_id')=? LIMIT 1""",

def settled_preexecution_rejection(connection, run_id, call):
    """Verify Core's pre-execution R0 denial without inventing a receipt."""
    try:
        from .tool_domain import CONTRACTS

        contract = next(item for item in CONTRACTS if item.name == call["tool_name"])
        if contract.risk != "R0" or call["state"] != "failed" or call["receipt_id"] is not None:
            return False
        result = json.loads(call["result_json"])
        if (
            result.get("state") != "rejected_before_execution"
            or result.get("call_id") != call["call_id"]
        ):
            return False
        if connection.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM action_intents WHERE call_id=?", (call["call_id"],)
        ).fetchone():
            return False
        event = connection.execute(
            "SELECT payload FROM events WHERE event_type='worker.progress' "
            "AND json_extract(payload,'$.run_id')=? AND json_extract(payload,'$.phase')='self_repair' "
            "AND json_extract(payload,'$.failed_call_id')=? AND json_extract(payload,'$.no_effect')=1 ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1",
            (run_id, call["call_id"]),
        ).fetchone()
        if event is None or json.loads(event[0]).get("parameter_digest") != parameter_digest(
            json.loads(call["arguments_json"])
        ):
            return False
        messages = connection.execute(
            "SELECT message_json FROM worker_messages WHERE run_id=? AND role='tool'", (run_id,)
        ).fetchall()
        return any(
            (item := json.loads(row[0])).get("tool_call_id") == call["model_call_id"]
            and json.loads(item["content"]).get("state") == "rejected_before_execution"
            for row in messages
        )
    except (StopIteration, TypeError, ValueError, KeyError, IndexError):
        return False

import hashlib

import os

from .domain import DomainError, ForgeEvent


def start(store, *, session_challenge):
    """Append a process generation while the caller owns the workspace lock."""
    if not isinstance(session_challenge, str) or not re.fullmatch(
        r"[0-9a-f]{64}", session_challenge
    ):
        raise DomainError("Invalid session challenge")
    generation = secrets.token_hex(16)
    with store.unit_of_work() as work:
        router = work.connection.execute(
            "SELECT router_session_id FROM router_state WHERE conversation_id='main'"
        ).fetchone()
        if router is None:
            raise DomainError("Router identity missing")
        work.append_event(
            ForgeEvent(
                event_type="core.started",
                payload={
                    "generation": generation,
                    "workspace_id": store.workspace.id,
                    "router_session_id": router["router_session_id"],
                    "pid": os.getpid(),
                    "session_challenge_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
                        session_challenge.encode()
                    ).hexdigest(),
                },
            )
        )
    return generation


def stop(store, generation):
    """Append a matching stop only for this process's recorded start."""
    if not isinstance(generation, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{32}", generation):
        raise DomainError("Invalid lifecycle generation")
    with store.unit_of_work() as work:
        row = work.connection.execute(
            "SELECT event_type,payload FROM events WHERE event_type IN ('core.started','core.stopped') AND json_extract(payload,'$.generation')=? ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1",
            (generation,),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise DomainError("Lifecycle start missing")
        payload = json.loads(row["payload"])
        if (
            row["event_type"] != "core.started"
            or payload.get("pid") != os.getpid()
            or payload.get("workspace_id") != store.workspace.id
        ):
            raise DomainError("Lifecycle stop does not match this process")
        work.append_event(ForgeEvent(event_type="core.stopped", payload=payload))

"""Bounded model semantic memory selection; never a source of new facts or authority."""

import hashlib
import json

from .domain import new_id
from .providers import ProviderError, ProviderGateway
from .runtime import ModelCallContext, ModelRequest


def _encoded(value):
    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def _digest(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(_encoded(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _candidate_refs(memory, cursor, candidate_limit):
    """Read a fixed range per index, without scanning every statement or doing I/O."""
    selectors = (
        ("memory_source_index", "source_ref", ""),
        ("memories", "id", "memory:"),
        ("constraint_records", "id", "constraint:"),
        ("constraint_message_index", "message_id", "message:"),
    )
    with memory._connection() as db:
        tables = {
            row[0]
            for row in db.execute(
                "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name IN "
                "('memory_source_index','memories','constraint_records','constraint_message_index')"
            )
        }
        refs = set()
        for table, identifier, prefix in selectors:
            if table not in tables:
                continue
            after = cursor or ""
            if prefix:
                if after.startswith(prefix):
                    after = after[len(prefix) :]
                elif after > prefix:
                    continue
                else:
                    after = ""
            # Identifiers and predicates above are fixed Core literals.
            # Range on the actual primary key, not a concatenation expression;
            # even revoked/stale records count against this page's read bound.
            refs.update(
                prefix + row[0]
                for row in db.execute(
                    f"SELECT {identifier} FROM {table} WHERE {identifier}>? "
                    f"ORDER BY {identifier} LIMIT ?",
                    (after, candidate_limit + 1),
                )
            )
    return sorted(refs)[: candidate_limit + 1]


async def retrieve_semantic_context(
    memory,
    query,

    capabilities=None,

):
    """Select source IDs by meaning, with one call and no model-derived evidence.

    Candidates are read from all indexed source classes independent of lexical
    overlap, so paraphrases can retrieve zero-word-overlap records. Candidate
    paging is explicit and stable; this is not an unbounded or learned index.
    """
    if (
        not isinstance(query, str)
        or not query.strip()
        or len(query.encode("utf-8")) > 8192
        or type(candidate_limit) is not int
        or not 1 <= candidate_limit <= 32
        or type(limit) is not int
        or not 1 <= limit <= candidate_limit
        or type(max_bytes) is not int
        or not 0 <= max_bytes <= 65536
        or type(context_limit) is not int
        or not 1024 <= context_limit <= 1_000_000
        or type(output_limit) is not int

        or (cursor is not None and (not isinstance(cursor, str) or len(cursor) > 600))

        raise ValueError("Invalid semantic recall bounds")
    allowed_filters = {
        "quest_ids",
        "kinds",
        "layers",
        "created_after",

        "source_types",
    }

"""Bounded model semantic memory selection; never a source of new facts or authority."""

import hashlib
import json

from .domain import new_id
from .providers import ProviderError, ProviderGateway
from .runtime import ModelCallContext, ModelRequest


def _encoded(value):
    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def _digest(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(_encoded(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _candidate_refs(memory, cursor, candidate_limit):
    """Read a fixed range per index, without scanning every statement or doing I/O."""
    selectors = (
        ("memory_source_index", "source_ref", ""),
        ("memories", "id", "memory:"),
        ("constraint_records", "id", "constraint:"),
        ("constraint_message_index", "message_id", "message:"),
    )
    with memory._connection() as db:
        tables = {
            row[0]
            for row in db.execute(
                "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name IN "
                "('memory_source_index','memories','constraint_records','constraint_message_index')"
            )
        }
        refs = set()
        for table, identifier, prefix in selectors:
            if table not in tables:
                continue
            after = cursor or ""
            if prefix:
                if after.startswith(prefix):
                    after = after[len(prefix) :]
                elif after > prefix:
                    continue
                else:
                    after = ""
            # Identifiers and predicates above are fixed Core literals.
            # Range on the actual primary key, not a concatenation expression;
            # even revoked/stale records count against this page's read bound.
            refs.update(
                prefix + row[0]
                for row in db.execute(
                    f"SELECT {identifier} FROM {table} WHERE {identifier}>? "
                    f"ORDER BY {identifier} LIMIT ?",
                    (after, candidate_limit + 1),
                )
            )
    return sorted(refs)[: candidate_limit + 1]


async def retrieve_semantic_context(
    memory,
    query,
    *,
    provider,
    model_id,
    provider_id=None,
    context_limit=16384,
    output_limit=512,
    quest_id=None,
    candidate_limit=24,
    limit=8,
    max_bytes=8192,
    cursor=None,
    capabilities=None,
    capability_sources=None,
    **filters,
):
    """Select source IDs by meaning, with one call and no model-derived evidence.

    Candidates are read from all indexed source classes independent of lexical
    overlap, so paraphrases can retrieve zero-word-overlap records. Candidate
    paging is explicit and stable; this is not an unbounded or learned index.
    """
    if (
        not isinstance(query, str)
        or not query.strip()
        or len(query.encode("utf-8")) > 8192
        or type(candidate_limit) is not int
        or not 1 <= candidate_limit <= 32
        or type(limit) is not int
        or not 1 <= limit <= candidate_limit
        or type(max_bytes) is not int
        or not 0 <= max_bytes <= 65536
        or type(context_limit) is not int
        or not 1024 <= context_limit <= 1_000_000
        or type(output_limit) is not int
        or not 64 <= output_limit <= 2048
        or (cursor is not None and (not isinstance(cursor, str) or len(cursor) > 600))
        or (quest_id is not None and (not isinstance(quest_id, str) or not quest_id))
    ):
        raise ValueError("Invalid semantic recall bounds")
    allowed_filters = {
        "quest_ids",
        "kinds",
        "layers",
        "created_after",
        "created_before",
        "source_types",
    }
"}

"""Conversational controls on an existing mandate, within the Router commit."""

from .domain import DomainError, ForgeEvent, now_iso


def control_task(work, quest, action, *, source_message_id):
    from .superagent_delegation import _active
    c = work.connection
    mandate = c.execute("SELECT id FROM delegation_mandates WHERE quest_id=?", (quest["id"],)).fetchone()
    if mandate is None:
        raise DomainError("Conversational control requires an autonomous task mandate")
    record, _policy = _active(c, mandate["id"], quest["id"])
    states = {
        "pause": {"approved": "paused", "queued": "paused", "running": "paused"},
        "resume": {"paused": "queued"},
        "cancel": {state: "cancelled" for state in ("proposed", "awaiting_approval", "approved",
                    "queued", "running", "paused", "blocked", "needs_input")},
    }
    target = states.get(action, {}).get(quest["status"])
    if target is None:
        raise DomainError("Task control is invalid in the current state")
    actor = "router_mandate:" + record["id"]
    changed = c.execute("UPDATE quests SET status=?,version=version+1,updated_at=? WHERE id=? AND version=?",
        (target, now_iso(), quest["id"], quest["version"]))
    if changed.rowcount != 1:
        raise DomainError("Task control lost its revision")
    plan_status = {"pause": "paused", "resume": "approved", "cancel": "cancelled"}[action]
    c.execute("UPDATE quest_plans SET status=? WHERE quest_id=? AND revision=? AND status IN ('proposed','approved','paused')",
              (plan_status, quest["id"], quest["plan_revision"]))
    work.append_event(ForgeEvent(event_type="quest.status_changed", quest_id=quest["id"],
        payload={"from": quest["status"], "to": target, "actor": actor, "source_message_id": source_message_id}))
    for row in c.execute("SELECT worker_id,plan_id,node_key FROM worker_runs WHERE quest_id=? "
                         "AND state IN ('queued','running','paused','blocked')", (quest["id"],)):
        work.append_event(ForgeEvent(event_type="worker.command." + action, quest_id=quest["id"],
            worker_id=row["worker_id"], payload={"plan_id": row["plan_id"], "task_node_key": row["node_key"],
                "actor": actor, "control_scope": "quest", "source_message_id": source_message_id}))

# Super-agent Capability Sprint

Date: 2026-11-16. Base: `57a162d31f9b559353fecbde61f95dd72f878abd`.
Branch: `codex/phase1-continuous`. Status: implementation and verification in progress.
No frontend work, architecture replacement, Git push or external Agent backend.

## Audit before implementation

The starting checkout was clean. README, STATUS, implementation report, source
and the preserved acceptance index were read first. STATUS still led with older
Phase 2 results; the actual baseline is the newer Super-agent implementation:
2312 passing tests, fourteen reproduced historical failures, two Windows skips,
and two bounded real scenarios with 39 settled calls. These historical successes
do not establish the more complex L1/L2/L3 required here.

Existing Worker inference/tools/checkpoints, DAG dependencies, source-verified
predecessor deliveries, partial replanning, model observations, Wilson intervals,
Registry discovery, compaction and governance are reused. Targeted starting
regression passed **104 tests** in `audit/superagent/capability-baseline.xml`.

| Sprint | Actual gap | Minimum change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Router context ignores project links; ambiguity spans projects; lifecycle controls stay outside conversation | Project-focused retrieval/candidates, source-bound project selection, coordination facts and conversational controls; same Router/CAS |
| B | Python tools cannot execute stdlib project tests; failed executable test result has no safe repair proof | Exact-manifest R2 CPython unittest tool, private cwd, process-tree cleanup, consumed approval proof and existing bounded repair loop |
| C | Autonomous contracts forbid dependencies although scheduler already supports them | Bounded coarse expert topology, verified handoffs, role-specific tools, source-bound help and bounded replacement/expansion |
| D | Identity discovery is not capability measurement; some health/outcome projections are absent | Extend existing performance projection and benchmark_runs with small attributed probes; keep unsupported dimensions unknown |
| E | Task-centric project isolation and long-term object retrieval need stronger tests | Project-filtered source retrieval and multi-hop/compaction continuity on existing records, preserving hashes and revocation |
| F | Healthy loop heartbeat does not establish Worker progress | Inspect actual checkpoints/settlements, emit deduplicated help with source references; retain lease/unknown-effect fences |
| G | Earlier live tasks were bounded file markers, not complex content/coding acceptance | New L1/L2/L3 with independent artifact checks and controlled strategy comparisons |

## Validation plan fixed before live execution

Real Provider runs use fresh isolated storage, the already authorized local proxy,
process-environment credentials and existing conservative 65536/4096 Router
context/output limits. Operator configuration is not edited. Each task keeps the
existing **32-call / 500000-token / 900-second** ceiling; no automatic Gateway
retry is added. A failed or uncertain run is retained and never replayed.

The planned task set is L1 project diagnosis, L2 source-based Agent-framework
research and L3 a small Python feature verified by real tests and independent
held-out cases. L2 also supplies a controlled single-Worker and fixed-team
comparison to the adaptive path: five task runs, at most 160 calls and 2500000
tokens in aggregate. Up to two discovered models may receive one six-dimension
microprobe suite each, separately capped at 16 calls / 100000 tokens. Unknown
prices remain unknown. Small samples support exploratory observations only.

One combined scenario must observe two distinct local project roots, concurrent
Workers, direct Thread follow-up, settled-boundary Core restart, actual context
compaction, typed Recall and delivery to the original Router. A model's claims,
mock fixtures and programmatic checks are recorded separately. Approved Python
code runs with the same OS account; private directories and fixed invocation do
not constitute an OS sandbox or a tamper-proof correctness oracle.

Final results, source freeze, test counts and unresolved limitations will be
added after verification; this document does not predeclare success.

# Super-agent experiments

Date: 2026-11-16. Capability Sprint base: `57a162d`.

## Protocol

The previous Super-agent audit and all Phase 2 experiments remain unchanged.
The new experiment set evaluates task outcomes, not model completion or apparent
progress. Fixed materials and independent acceptance checks are held constant
across single, fixed and adaptive team interventions. No algorithm is assumed
optimal. Model routing compares eligible discovered identities only; identity
discovery is not a measured capability score.

Task-centric context is evaluated through project-isolation mutation tests and
the combined real two-project/restart/compaction/Recall scenario. Recovery tests
inject known infrastructure failures and unknown effects separately; successful
recovery requires preserved evidence and no duplicate uncertain operation.

Collect: task success, settled/unknown calls, input/output/charged tokens, cost
when trusted prices exist, elapsed time, tool counts, self-repair/review rework,
recovery success, source citations and evidence completeness. All denominators,
sample sizes, execution modes and source hashes must be recorded. Real model
results, scripted model protocols and programmatic filesystem/runtime checks
are separate evidence classes.

## Current status

Execution is in progress. No current-sprint live success or comparative advantage
is claimed until the corresponding retained report has passed final accounting
and independent content/artifact checks. Per-task ceilings are fixed in the
[Sprint report](SUPERAGENT_CAPABILITY_SPRINT_REPORT.md).
