format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: exec

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.
tools.name: request_user_input

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.
tools.name: request_user_input_async

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.
tools.name: clock

tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.
tools.name: sleep

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.
tools.name: collaboration

tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.
tools.name: followup_task

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.
tools.name: interrupt_agent

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.
tools.name: list_agents

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.
tools.name: send_message

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.
tools.name: spawn_agent

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.
tools.name: wait_agent

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.
tools.name: mcp__cua_repl

tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

我们需要纠正 FORGE 的架构方向。你自己设定一个目标，不断推进。

本项目真正的目标是：**自主研发一套通用版 DeepSeek Super-agent，而不是普通 Agent、Agent 管理平台或简单的 Multi-Agent 框架。**

请将 DeepSeek Harness 团队的《Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System》作为核心架构依据，并深入研究官方原型：

[https://github.com/DeepSeek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype](https://github.com/DeepSeek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype)

同时研究：

- [https://github.com/openai/codex](https://github.com/openai/codex)
- [https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code)

Codex 和 Claude Code 主要用于研究底层 Harness、工具执行、上下文压缩和权限设计；**DeepSeek Super-agent 才是 FORGE 的总体架构目标。**

### 必须实现的核心架构

1. Persistent Router：一个长期存在的主 Session，负责所有用户交互、全局记忆和任务协调。
2. Isolated Workers：每项独立任务使用独立 Worker Session 和执行环境，Worker 不直接与用户交互。
3. Event-driven Triggers：支持用户消息、定时任务、文件变化、任务结果及外部事件；实现 Fast Path 和 Slow Path 两级过滤。
4. Thread Subscription & Pass-through：同一任务后续事件直接路由到对应 Worker，避免所有事件都经过 Router 推理。
5. Inline & Spill：合理控制上下文，把必要信息内联，完整内容保留在外部存储并按需读取。
6. Chain of Recall：通过对象引用关系恢复历史任务、项目状态、决策和执行记录。
7. Persistent State：Conversation、Router、Worker、Quest 和 Event 均可持久化与恢复。
8. Watchdog：监控 Router、Worker、Dispatcher 和执行环境，处理异常退出、超时及恢复。

### FORGE 自己的扩展

- 通用 Workspace 自动识别和关联，不局限于 GitHub。
- Model Intelligence Registry：管理模型的数学、编程、设计、研究、推理、速度和成本属性。
- Adaptive Team Composition：Router 根据任务动态选择模型、角色和 Worker 数量。
- 本地优先，支持终端、文件、浏览器、Git、MCP 和 GPU 等工具。
- 统一对话入口，所有 Worker 结果由 Router 汇总。

### 重构要求

先深入阅读 DeepSeek 论文、官方原型的文档和源码，逐模块对比当前 FORGE。

重点审查现有 Router、Worker Runtime、Dispatcher、Event、Context、Memory 和 Watchdog 实现。

不要推倒重写，也不要为了架构图增加无意义的 Manager。保留已经可靠的数据库事务、CAS、Outbox、权限和证据机制。

前端目前效果不错，保持现有前端不变，主要重构后端。

允许连续实施，不必每个小阶段等待确认。每次重构都必须有测试和真实 Provider 验证。

### 最终验收

用户只与一个长期存在的 FORGE 对话。

FORGE 能够持续接收事件、理解任务、自动创建和管理多个隐藏 Worker、订阅后续事件、并行执行、主动恢复失败，并通过 Chain of Recall 保持跨项目连续性。

用户不需要管理 Session，不需要手动分配 Agent，也不需要频繁重新解释任务。

请先完成架构差异审计，再制定最小改动的重构计划，然后直接实施。

**不要再把 FORGE 做成 Quest/DAG/Approval 管理平台。它们只是 Super-agent 的内部基础设施。核心产品是一个持续运行、主动工作、能够组织多个 Worker 的 Super-agent。**
把代码提交到github吧

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.

## 本轮总目标

让 FORGE 从已经具备 Super-agent 架构的工程，进化为真正能够长期自主工作的通用 Super-agent。

重点完善以下能力：

### 1. Router Intelligence

- 提升多 Workspace 意图识别和 Quest 关联准确率。
- 支持多个并行任务的持续协调。
- 优化事件批处理，减少不必要的模型调用。
- 支持任务优先级、阻塞判断和主动进度汇报。
- 支持对 Worker 结果进行判断、追问、重新委派和终止。
- 避免 Router 退化为纯任务登记器或简单转发器。

### 2. Worker Autonomy

- Worker 应具备真正独立的模型推理和工具调用循环。
- 完善复杂任务内部的子任务规划与依赖管理。
- 支持有界的专家协作和动态扩展。
- 完善错误分类、策略调整、有限重试和失败求助。
- 支持暂停、恢复、取消、崩溃恢复。
- 不允许通过无限增加 Token、输出长度或重试次数解决问题。

### 3. Adaptive Agent Swarm

重点提升动态组队质量，而不是固定启动六个角色。

支持：

- Single Worker
- Parallel Specialists
- Sequential Specialists
- Hierarchical Team
- Dynamic Expansion
- Model Replacement

Router 根据任务复杂度、能力需求、模型可靠性、工具兼容性、成本和延迟决定是否组队。

保留单 Agent 基线，并通过真实任务比较不同组队策略。不要预先宣称某种算法最优。

### 4. Model Intelligence

强化现有 Model Registry：

- 自动发现可用模型及其能力。
- 测量实际延迟、吞吐量和失败率。
- 统计真实任务成功率、工具成功率和 Reviewer 通过率。
- 建立数学、编程、研究、设计、视觉、规划等能力评测。
- 记录来源、样本量、测量时间和置信度。
- 支持任务级动态选模和模型故障切换。

优先使用已经授权的本地 Provider 和真实模型。

不得打印密钥，不得修改用户原有 Provider 配置，不得无限增加模型预算。

### 5. Workspace & Chain of Recall

- 增强跨项目自动识别。
- 多 Workspace 记忆隔离。
- 支持跨 Quest、Worker、Artifact 和历史决策检索。
- 优化多跳 Recall。
- 支持长期对话的上下文恢复。
- 保证压缩后原始证据仍然可以追溯。

用户始终只使用一个对话入口。

### 6. Watchdog & Self-Recovery

在现有 Watchdog 上继续完善：

- Worker 卡死识别。
- 任务长期无进展检测。
- Provider 故障检测。
- 执行环境异常检测。
- 过期租约恢复。

user_messages.text:
我们需要纠正 FORGE 的架构方向。你自己设定一个目标，不断推进。

本项目真正的目标是：**自主研发一套通用版 DeepSeek Super-agent，而不是普通 Agent、Agent 管理平台或简单的 Multi-Agent 框架。**

请将 DeepSeek Harness 团队的《Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System》作为核心架构依据，并深入研究官方原型：

[https://github.com/DeepSeek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype](https://github.com/DeepSeek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype)

同时研究：

- [https://github.com/openai/codex](https://github.com/openai/codex)
- [https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code)

Codex 和 Claude Code 主要用于研究底层 Harness、工具执行、上下文压缩和权限设计；**DeepSeek Super-agent 才是 FORGE 的总体架构目标。**

### 必须实现的核心架构

1. Persistent Router：一个长期存在的主 Session，负责所有用户交互、全局记忆和任务协调。
2. Isolated Workers：每项独立任务使用独立 Worker Session 和执行环境，Worker 不直接与用户交互。
3. Event-driven Triggers：支持用户消息、定时任务、文件变化、任务结果及外部事件；实现 Fast Path 和 Slow Path 两级过滤。
4. Thread Subscription & Pass-through：同一任务后续事件直接路由到对应 Worker，避免所有事件都经过 Router 推理。
5. Inline & Spill：合理控制上下文，把必要信息内联，完整内容保留在外部存储并按需读取。
6. Chain of Recall：通过对象引用关系恢复历史任务、项目状态、决策和执行记录。
7. Persistent State：Conversation、Router、Worker、Quest 和 Event 均可持久化与恢复。
8. Watchdog：监控 Router、Worker、Dispatcher 和执行环境，处理异常退出、超时及恢复。

### FORGE 自己的扩展

- 通用 Workspace 自动识别和关联，不局限于 GitHub。
- Model Intelligence Registry：管理模型的数学、编程、设计、研究、推理、速度和成本属性。
- Adaptive Team Composition：Router 根据任务动态选择模型、角色和 Worker 数量。
- 本地优先，支持终端、文件、浏览器、Git、MCP 和 GPU 等工具。
- 统一对话入口，所有 Worker 结果由 Router 汇总。

### 重构要求

先深入阅读 DeepSeek 论文、官方原型的文档和源码，逐模块对比当前 FORGE。

重点审查现有 Router、Worker Runtime、Dispatcher、Event、Context、Memory 和 Watchdog 实现。

不要推倒重写，也不要为了架构图增加无意义的 Manager。保留已经可靠的数据库事务、CAS、Outbox、权限和证据机制。

前端目前效果不错，保持现有前端不变，主要重构后端。

允许连续实施，不必每个小阶段等待确认。每次重构都必须有测试和真实 Provider 验证。

### 最终验收

用户只与一个长期存在的 FORGE 对话。

FORGE 能够持续接收事件、理解任务、自动创建和管理多个隐藏 Worker、订阅后续事件、并行执行、主动恢复失败，并通过 Chain of Recall 保持跨项目连续性。

用户不需要管理 Session，不需要手动分配 Agent，也不需要频繁重新解释任务。

请先完成架构差异审计，再制定最小改动的重构计划，然后直接实施。

**不要再把 FORGE 做成 Quest/DAG/Approval 管理平台。它们只是 Super-agent 的内部基础设施。核心产品是一个持续运行、主动工作、能够组织多个 Worker 的 Super-agent。**
把代码提交到github吧

# FORGE — Super-agent Capability Sprint

## Continue from current branch and current implementation

继续当前 FORGE 项目，不要新建项目，不要重置上下文，不要重新设计 Architecture v5。

当前分支：`codex/phase1-continuous`

## 本轮总目标

让 FORGE 从已经具备 Super-agent 架构的工程，进化为真正能够长期自主工作的通用 Super-agent。

重点完善以下能力：

### 1. Router Intelligence

- 提升多 Workspace 意图识别和 Quest 关联准确率。
- 支持多个并行任务的持续协调。
- 优化事件批处理，减少不必要的模型调用。
- 支持任务优先级、阻塞判断和主动进度汇报。
- 支持对 Worker 结果进行判断、追问、重新委派和终止。
- 避免 Router 退化为纯任务登记器或简单转发器。

### 2. Worker Autonomy

- Worker 应具备真正独立的模型推理和工具调用循环。
- 完善复杂任务内部的子任务规划与依赖管理。
- 支持有界的专家协作和动态扩展。
- 完善错误分类、策略调整、有限重试和失败求助。
- 支持暂停、恢复、取消、崩溃恢复。
- 不允许通过无限增加 Token、输出长度或重试次数解决问题。

### <truncated omitted_approx_tokens="899" />加专家，最终交付真实代码和测试证据。

至少一个场景必须验证：

- 两个独立 Workspace。
- 多个并行 Worker。
- Thread Subscription / Pass-through。
- Core 中途重启。
- Context Compaction。
- Chain of Recall。
- 最终结果回传原始 Router。

真实模型调用、Mock、程序化测试必须分别标记。

## 研究要求

对 Adaptive Team Composition、Task-Centric Context、Self-Recovery 建立可复现评测。

比较单 Agent、固定团队、动态团队和不同模型路由策略。

记录任务成功率、成本、延迟、Token、工具调用、返工次数、恢复成功率和证据完整率。

小样本结果只报告探索性结论，不夸大效果。

## 严格约束

- 不推翻当前 Super-agent 架构。
- 不重做前端 UI。
- 不重新建立数据库或平行状态系统。
- 保留 Milestone 1 的事务、CAS、Outbox。
- 保留当前治理、审批、证据和预算边界。
- 不使用 Codex、DSH、Claude Code 作为执行后端。
- 不使用虚假模型结果或模拟进度冒充真实执行。
- 不自动推送 GitHub。
- 不删除历史失败实验和审计记录。
- 不通过扩大预算、上下文或重试次数掩盖架构缺陷。

# FORGE v4 — General-purpose Super-agent

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose DeepSeek-style Super-agent desktop
application: one persistent Router conversation coordinates hidden, isolated
Workers and continuously receives events.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-16

The backend architecture now follows DeepSeek Super-agent's
persistent Router and independent Workers. The default Core delegates ordinary
conversational tasks automatically, filters environmental events, sends Thread
continuations directly to subscribed Workers, follows typed Chain of Recall
references, and supervises durable execution. Plans, Quests and approval records
are internal infrastructure. The frontend is unchanged in this correction.

Read the [architecture audit and refactor plan](docs/SUPERAGENT_REFACTOR_PLAN.md),
[product architecture](docs/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[implementation and validation report](docs/SUPERAGENT_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md)
for the exact implemented behavior, tests, real Provider observations and limits.
Historical Phase 2 evidence remains available below; it does not describe the
new autonomous dispatch path.

Frozen-source real Provider acceptance passed both the
[conversational/restart scenario](docs/audit/superagent/20261115T193658Z-d72209.json)
and the [event/adaptive-team scenario](docs/audit/superagent/20261115T193938Z-cold-697d50.json),
with 22/22 and 17/17 calls settled respectively. These bounded observations
verify the new backend flow; exact tool limits and regression debt are recorded
in the implementation report and do not establish arbitrary-task correctness.
The frozen backend regression recorded **2312 passed, 14 failed, 2 skipped**;
the fourteen failures match those reproduced on the base source and tests.
See the [acceptance index](docs/audit/superagent/acceptance-index.json) for
report hashes, final evidence and preserved diagnostic history.

See the [current status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),
[experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [V22 historical boundary](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v22-boundary.md).
Historical failures and original evidence remain preserved. The real algorithm
microstudy scored 25/90 task successes; it does not establish general policy gains.
Frontend work is being handled separately; packaging is outside this sprint.

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. DeepSeek Super-agent defines the overall architecture; Codex and Claude Code inform Harness design. None is an execution backend.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering implementation with bounded context recovery, source-bound
recall and evidence-gated execution. A configured Provider is required; Mock
tests and real Provider observations are identified separately. Autonomous
internal plan/team contracts use an auditable host mandate tied to the original
request or admitted Trigger. Manual approvals retain authenticated user authority,
and risky tool actions still require their own authorization. A mandate or
proposal does not prove execution. Worker directories are private execution
contexts, not an OS sandbox. General complex-task correctness remains subject to
recorded acceptance.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` | Defaults to `false`: cumulative workspace, Quest, team and Worker token estimates do not stop execution. Usage is still recorded and unsettled calls remain unresolved. Set `true` to opt into cumulative limits and configure `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT`. Model context/output limits, concurrency, tool permissions, deadlines and review counts still apply. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |

# Super-agent Capability Sprint

Date: 2026-11-16. Base: `57a162d31f9b559353fecbde61f95dd72f878abd`.
Branch: `codex/phase1-continuous`. Status: implementation and verification in progress.
No frontend work, architecture replacement, Git push or external Agent backend.

## Audit before implementation

The starting checkout was clean. README, STATUS, implementation report, source
and the preserved acceptance index were read first. STATUS still led with older
Phase 2 results; the actual baseline is the newer Super-agent implementation:
2312 passing tests, fourteen reproduced historical failures, two Windows skips,
and two bounded real scenarios with 39 settled calls. These historical successes
do not establish the more complex L1/L2/L3 required here.

Existing Worker inference/tools/checkpoints, DAG dependencies, source-verified
predecessor deliveries, partial replanning, model observations, Wilson intervals,
Registry discovery, compaction and governance are reused. Targeted starting
regression passed **104 tests** in `audit/superagent/capability-baseline.xml`.

| Sprint | Actual gap | Minimum change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Router context ignores project links; ambiguity spans projects; lifecycle controls stay outside conversation | Project-focused retrieval/candidates, source-bound project selection, coordination facts and conversational controls; same Router/CAS |
| B | Python tools cannot execute stdlib project tests; failed executable test result has no safe repair proof | Exact-manifest R2 CPython unittest tool, private cwd, process-tree cleanup, consumed approval proof and existing bounded repair loop |
| C | Autonomous contracts forbid dependencies although scheduler already supports them | Bounded coarse expert topology, verified handoffs, role-specific tools, source-bound help and bounded replacement/expansion |
| D | Identity discovery is not capability measurement; some health/outcome projections are absent | Extend existing performance projection and benchmark_runs with small attributed probes; keep unsupported dimensions unknown |
| E | Task-centric project isolation and long-term object retrieval need stronger tests | Project-filtered source retrieval and multi-hop/compaction continuity on existing records, preserving hashes and revocation |
| F | Healthy loop heartbeat does not establish Worker progress | Inspect actual checkpoints/settlements, emit deduplicated help with source references; retain lease/unknown-effect fences |
| G | Earlier live tasks were bounded file markers, not complex content/coding acceptance | New L1/L2/L3 with independent artifact checks and controlled strategy comparisons |

## Validation plan fixed before live execution

Real Provider runs use fresh isolated storage, the already authorized local proxy,
process-environment credentials and existing conservative 65536/4096 Router
context/output limits. Operator configuration is not edited. Each task keeps the
existing **32-call / 500000-token / 900-second** ceiling; no automatic Gateway
retry is added. A failed or uncertain run is retained and never replayed.

The planned task set is L1 project diagnosis, L2 source-based Agent-framework
research and L3 a small Python feature verified by real tests and independent
held-out cases. L2 also supplies a controlled single-Worker and fixed-team
comparison to the adaptive path: five task runs, at most 160 calls and 2500000
tokens in aggregate. Up to two discovered models may receive one six-dimension
microprobe suite each, separately capped at 16 calls / 100000 tokens. Unknown
prices remain unknown. Small samples support exploratory observations only.

One combined scenario must observe two distinct local project roots, concurrent
Workers, direct Thread follow-up, settled-boundary Core restart, actual context
compaction, typed Recall and delivery to the original Router. A model's claims,
mock fixtures and programmatic checks are recorded separately. Approved Python
code runs with the same OS account; private directories and fixed invocation do
not constitute an OS sandbox or a tamper-proof correctness oracle.

Final results, source freeze, test counts and unresolved limitations will be
added after verification; this document does not predeclare success.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. DeepSeek Super-agent defines the overall architecture; Codex and Claude Code inform Harness design. None is an execution backend.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering implementation with bounded context recovery, source-bound
recall and evidence-gated execution. A configured Provider is required; Mock
tests and real Provider observations are identified separately. Autonomous
internal plan/team contracts use an auditable host mandate tied to the original
request or admitted Trigger. Manual approvals retain authenticated user authority,
and risky tool actions still require their own authorization. A mandate or
proposal does not prove execution. Worker directories are private execution
contexts, not an OS sandbox. General complex-task correctness remains subject to
recorded acceptance.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` | Defaults to `false`: cumulative workspace, Quest, team and Worker token estimates do not stop execution. Usage is still recorded and unsettled calls remain unresolved. Set `true` to opt into cumulative limits and configure `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT`. Model context/output limits, concurrency, tool permissions, deadlines and review counts still apply. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |

## Audit before implementation

The starting checkout was clean. README, STATUS, implementation report, source
and the preserved acceptance index were read first. STATUS still led with older
Phase 2 results; the actual baseline is the newer Super-agent implementation:
2312 passing tests, fourteen reproduced historical failures, two Windows skips,

do not establish the more complex L1/L2/L3 required here.

Existing Worker inference/tools/checkpoints, DAG dependencies, source-verified
predecessor deliveries, partial replanning, model observations, Wilson intervals,

regression passed **104 tests** in `audit/superagent/capability-baseline.xml`.

| Sprint | Actual gap | Minimum change |
| --- | --- | --- |

| B | Python tools cannot execute stdlib project tests; failed executable test result has no safe repair proof | Exact-manifest R2 CPython unittest tool, private cwd, process-tree cleanup, consumed approval proof and existing bounded repair loop |
| C | Autonomous contracts forbid dependencies although scheduler already supports them | Bounded coarse expert topology, verified handoffs, role-specific tools, source-bound help and bounded replacement/expansion |
| D | Identity discovery is not capability measurement; some health/outcome projections are absent | Extend existing performance projection and benchmark_runs with small attributed probes; keep unsupported dimensions unknown |
| E | Task-centric project isolation and long-term object retrieval need stronger tests | Project-filtered source retrieval and multi-hop/compaction continuity on existing records, preserving hashes and revocation |
| F | Healthy loop heartbeat does not establish Worker progress | Inspect actual checkpoints/settlements, emit deduplicated help with source references; retain lease/unknown-effect fences |
| G | Earlier live tasks were bounded file markers, not complex content/coding acceptance | New L1/L2/L3 with independent artifact checks and controlled strategy comparisons |

## Validation plan fixed before live execution

Real Provider runs use fresh isolated storage, the already authorized local proxy,
process-environment credentials and existing conservative 65536/4096 Router
context/output limits. Operator configuration is not edited. Each task keeps the
existing **32-call / 500000-token / 900-second** ceiling; no automatic Gateway
retry is added. A failed or uncertain run is retained and never replayed.

The planned task set is L1 project diagnosis, L2 source-based Agent-framework
research and L3 a small Python feature verified by real tests and independent
held-out cases. L2 also supplies a controlled single-Worker and fixed-team
comparison to the adaptive path: five task runs, at most 160 calls and 2500000
tokens in aggregate. Up to two discovered models may receive one six-dimension
microprobe suite each, separately capped at 16 calls / 100000 tokens. Unknown
prices remain unknown. Small samples support exploratory observations only.

One combined scenario must observe two distinct local project roots, concurrent
Workers, direct Thread follow-up, settled-boundary Core restart, actual context
compaction, typed Recall and delivery to the original Router. A model's claims,
mock fixtures and programmatic checks are recorded separately. Approved Python
code runs with the same OS account; private directories and fixed invocation do
not constitute an OS sandbox or a tamper-proof correctness oracle.

"""Bounded real-Provider acceptance through a fresh Core's authenticated API.

Supply the Provider credential in the process environment; this driver never
reads operator credential files. Published JSON contains allowlisted assertions,
usage and hashes, never raw prompts/replies, logs, secrets or database contents.
Offline tests are separate and are never reported as live success here.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import secrets
import sqlite3
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from contextlib import closing
from copy import deepcopy
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "phase2"))

import live_core

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
NOTICE_TYPES = (
    "worker.blocked",
    "worker.failed",
    "worker.result",
    "worker.help_requested",
    "approval.requested",
    "worker.command.cancel",
    "worker.progress",
    "quest.status_changed",
)


class ProbeFailure(RuntimeError):
    pass


def source_digest():
    result = hashlib.sha256()
    files = sorted((REPO / "backend" / "src").rglob("*.py")) + [Path(__file__)]
    for path in files:
        result.update(str(path.relative_to(REPO)).replace("\\", "/").encode())
        result.update(path.read_bytes())
    return result.hexdigest()


def snapshot(path):
    with closing(
        sqlite3.connect(f"{Path(path).as_uri()}?mode=ro", uri=True, timeout=5)
    ) as connection:
        connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        rows = lambda sql: [dict(row) for row in connection.execute(sql)]
        messages = rows("SELECT id,role,content,metadata FROM messages ORDER BY rowid")
        return {
            "router": rows("SELECT router_session_id FROM router_state")[0]["router_session_id"],
            "quests": rows("SELECT id,status FROM quests ORDER BY rowid"),
            "workers": rows(
                "SELECT id,quest_id,worker_id,state,execution_mode FROM worker_runs ORDER BY rowid"
            ),
            "hidden": rows("SELECT hidden FROM workers"),
            "request_quests": rows(
                "SELECT q.id,json_extract(m.metadata,'$.request_id') AS request_id "
                "FROM quests q JOIN messages m "
                "ON m.id=json_extract(q.metadata,'$.original_request_message_id')"
            ),
            "subscriptions": rows("SELECT run_id,active FROM superagent_subscriptions"),
            "core_reads": rows(
                "SELECT run_id,tool_name,state FROM worker_tool_calls "
                "WHERE tool_name IN ('read_trigger','recall_object')"
            ),
            "calls": rows(
                "SELECT purpose,state,created_at,input_charged,output_charged "
                "FROM model_budget_attempts ORDER BY created_at"
            ),
            "receipts": rows(
                "SELECT i.run_id,i.tool_name,i.resource_scope,r.execution_mode,r.result_json FROM action_receipts r "
                "JOIN action_intents i ON i.id=r.intent_id WHERE i.state='succeeded'"
            ),
            "events": rows(
                "SELECT id,event_type,quest_id,payload,created_at FROM events ORDER BY seq"
            ),
            "router_notices": [
                dict(row)
                for row in connection.execute(
                    "SELECT e.id,i.processed_at,i.notice_dead_at FROM events e "
                    "LEFT JOIN event_inbox i ON i.event_id=e.id AND i.consumer_id='router' "
                    "WHERE e.event_type IN (" + ",".join("?" for _ in NOTICE_TYPES) + ")",
                    NOTICE_TYPES,
                )
            ],
            "messages": messages,
            "message_digest": hashlib.sha256(
                json.dumps(messages, sort_keys=True).encode()
            ).hexdigest(),
        }


def call(core, method, route, payload=None):
    result = core.call(method, route, payload, timeout=180)
    if result["status"] != 200:
        raise ProbeFailure(f"api_status_{result['status']}")
    return result["body"]


def notices_for_tasks(state):
    events = {event["id"]: event for event in state["events"]}
    result = set()
    for message in state["messages"]:
        metadata = json.loads(message["metadata"])
        event = events.get(metadata.get("event_id"))
        if (
            metadata.get("source") == "router_notice"
            and event
            and (
                event["event_type"] in {"worker.result", "quest.completed", "task.verified"}
                or (
                    event["event_type"] == "quest.status_changed"
                    and json.loads(event["payload"]).get("to") == "completed"
                )
            )
        ):
            result.add(event["quest_id"])
    return result


def guard_bounds(state, args):
    if len(state["calls"]) >= args.max_calls:
        raise ProbeFailure("model_call_ceiling_reached")
    if any(call["state"] in {"uncertain", "unknown"} for call in state["calls"]):
        raise ProbeFailure("unknown_provider_outcome")
    if any(
        call["state"] != "settled" and time.time() - call["created_at"] > 150
        for call in state["calls"]
    ):
        raise ProbeFailure("unsettled_provider_timeout")


def quiescent_since(state, ready, previous, *, now=None):
    """Require drained Router deliveries and an unchanged settled snapshot for 2s."""
    if any(item["notice_dead_at"] is not None for item in state["router_notices"]):
        raise ProbeFailure("router_notice_dead_lettered")
    if (
        not ready
        or any(item["state"] != "settled" for item in state["calls"])
        or any(item["processed_at"] is None for item in state["router_notices"])
    ):
        return None, False
    now = time.monotonic() if now is None else now
    signature = (len(state["calls"]), len(state["events"]), state["message_digest"])
    since = previous[1] if previous is not None and previous[0] == signature else now
    return (signature, since), now - since >= 2


def running_intervals(state):
    """Observed ownership intervals, not continuous compute or CPU utilization.

    A repeated claim without a durable closing fact cannot erase the earlier
    ownership observation. Provider-capacity waits may occur inside an interval.
    """
    active, intervals = {}, []
    closes = {
        "worker.result",
        "worker.blocked",
        "worker.failed",
        "worker.paused",
        "worker.cancelled",
    }
    for event in state["events"]:
        run_id = json.loads(event["payload"]).get("run_id")
        if not run_id:
            continue
        if event["event_type"] == "worker.accepted":
            active.setdefault(run_id, event["created_at"])
        elif event["event_type"] in closes and run_id in active:
            intervals.append(
                {
                    "run_id": run_id,
                    "started_at": active.pop(run_id),
                    "ended_at": event["created_at"],
                }
            )
    boundaries = sorted(
        (stamp, change)
        for item in intervals
        for stamp, change in ((item["started_at"], 1), (item["ended_at"], -1))
    )
    current, maximum = 0, 0
    for _, change in boundaries:
        current += change
        maximum = max(maximum, current)
    return intervals, maximum


def final_accounting(report, state):
    settled = all(item["state"] == "settled" for item in state["calls"])
    drained = all(
        item["processed_at"] is not None and item["notice_dead_at"] is None
        for item in state["router_notices"]
    )
    report["checks"]["final_provider_calls_settled"] = settled
    report["checks"]["final_router_deliveries_drained"] = drained
    if not settled or not drained:
        report["status"] = "failed"
        report.setdefault("failure_code", "final_provider_or_router_work_unsettled")


def verified_artifact(state, workspace, quest_id, expected_marker):
    run_ids = {worker["id"] for worker in state["workers"] if worker["quest_id"] == quest_id}
    for receipt in state["receipts"]:
        if receipt["run_id"] not in run_ids or receipt["tool_name"] not in {
            "file_write",
            "file_revise",
        }:
            continue
        path = Path(receipt["resource_scope"]).resolve()
        if not path.is_relative_to(workspace.resolve()) or not path.is_file():
            continue
        data = path.read_bytes()
        digest = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        if (
            expected_marker.encode() not in data
            or json.loads(receipt["result_json"]).get("sha256") != digest
        ):
            continue
        if any(
            read["run_id"] in run_ids
            and read["tool_name"] == "file_read"
            and read["resource_scope"] == receipt["resource_scope"]
            and json.loads(read["result_json"]).get("sha256") == digest
            for read in state["receipts"]
        ):
            return True
    return False

"""Phase 2 live Core harness: spawn an isolated Core, authenticate, drive the API.

Credential handling: the provider key is read from a process environment variable
named by FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF. Nothing secret is written to disk or logs.

import hashlib
import hmac
import os
import secrets
import socket

import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

def free_port():
    with socket.socket() as sock:
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return sock.getsockname()[1]


class LiveCore:
    def __init__(
        self, workspace, *, provider_env, token_limit, concurrency, log=None, extra_env=None
    ):
        if token_limit is not None and (type(token_limit) is not int or token_limit < 1):
            raise ValueError("token_limit must be a positive integer or None")

        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}"

        self.bearer = None
        self.process = None
        self.provider_env = provider_env
        self.token_limit = token_limit
        self.concurrency = concurrency
        self.log_path = log or self.workspace / "core.log"
        self.extra_env = extra_env or {}
        self.stdout = None

    def env(self):
        raw = bytes.fromhex(self.secret)
        assert len(raw) == 32
        values = {
            "FORGE_WORKSPACE_ROOT": str(self.workspace),
            "FORGE_DB_PATH": "data/forge.sqlite3",
            "FORGE_HOST": "127.0.0.1",
            "FORGE_PORT": str(self.port),
            "FORGE_CORE_SECRET": self.secret,
            "FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID": MODEL_ID,
            "FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT": "65536",
            "FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE": "4096",
            "FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS": "150",
            "FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS": "3",
            "FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS": "false" if self.token_limit is None else "true",
            "FORGE_MODEL_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT": str(self.concurrency),
            "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8",
            "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1",
        }
        if self.token_limit is not None:
            values["FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT"] = str(self.token_limit)
        values.update(self.provider_env)
        values.update(self.extra_env)
        expected_policy = "false" if self.token_limit is None else "true"
        if values.get("FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS") != expected_policy:
            raise ValueError("Token budget policy conflicts with token_limit")
        if self.token_limit is None:
            if "FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT" in values:
                raise ValueError("Disabled token budgets must omit FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT")
        else:
            try:
                configured_limit = int(values["FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT"])
            except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
                raise ValueError("Invalid model token limit") from exc
            if configured_limit < 1 or configured_limit > self.token_limit:
                raise ValueError("Model token limit must stay within the harness limit")
        base = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith("FORGE_")}
        base.update(values)
        return base

    def start(self, timeout=120):
        # Kept open for the child lifetime and closed by stop(), including failures.
        self.stdout = open(self.log_path, "ab")  # noqa: SIM115
        env = self.env()
        creation = 0
        if os.name == "nt":
            creation = subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
            [str(PYTHON), "-m", "forge_api", "--workspace-root", str(self.workspace)],
            cwd=str(BACKEND),
            env=env,
            stdout=self.stdout,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            creationflags=creation,
        )
        deadline = time.time() + timeout
        while time.time() < deadline:
            if self.process.poll() is not None:
                raise RuntimeError("Core exited during startup")
            try:
                response = httpx.get(self.base_url + "/health", timeout=2, trust_env=False)
                if response.status_code == 200:
                    self.session = response.json()["session"]
                    raw = bytes.fromhex(self.secret)
                    self.bearer = hmac.new(raw, self.session.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
                    return self
            except (httpx.TransportError, httpx.TimeoutException):
                pass
            time.sleep(0.25)
        raise RuntimeError("Core did not become healthy")

    def client(self, timeout=240):
        return httpx.Client(
            base_url=self.base_url,
            headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + self.bearer},
            timeout=httpx.Timeout(connect=5, read=timeout, write=10, pool=5),
            trust_env=False,
            follow_redirects=False,
        )

    def call(self, method, path, payload=None, timeout=240):
        with self.client(timeout=timeout) as client:
            response = client.request(method, path, json=payload)
        try:
            body = response.json()
        except ValueError:
            body = {"raw": response.text[:400]}
        return {"status": response.status_code, "body": body}

    def stop(self, *, graceful=True):
        if self.process is None:
            return
        if self.process.poll() is None:
            if graceful:
                self.process.terminate()
            else:
                self.process.kill()
            try:
                self.process.wait(timeout=30)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                self.process.kill()
                self.process.wait(timeout=15)
        if self.stdout:
            self.stdout.close()
            self.stdout = None

    def tail_log(self, limit=4000):
        if not self.log_path.exists():
            return ""
        data = self.log_path.read_bytes()[-limit:]
        return data.decode("utf-8", "replace")

"""Scripted Router decisions against real multi-project state, not live models."""

import asyncio
import json

import pytest

from test_router_responsiveness_superagent import background_task
from test_superagent_loop import MockProvider, conversational_decision, response
from test_superagent_loop import rig as base_rig

from forge_core.context_service import ContextService
from forge_core.domain import ConversationMessage
from forge_core.router_domain import ExecutionTeam, RouterDecision
from forge_core.workspace_discovery import WorkspaceDiscovery


@pytest.fixture
def rig(tmp_path):
    store, router, triggers = base_rig.__wrapped__(tmp_path)
    projects = []
    for name in ("alpha_project", "beta_project"):
        path = tmp_path / name
        path.mkdir()
        (path / "pyproject.toml").write_text("[project]\nname='" + name + "'\n", encoding="utf-8")
        quest, _worker = background_task(store)
        projects.append((quest, WorkspaceDiscovery(store).associate(quest.id, path)))
    return store, router, triggers, projects


def test_focused_recall_excludes_other_project_constraints(rig):
    store, router, _triggers, projects = rig
    for (quest, project), marker in zip(projects, ("ALPHA_PRIVATE", "BETA_PRIVATE"), strict=True):
        source = ConversationMessage(role="user", content="shared-rule " + marker)
        with store.unit_of_work() as work:
            work.add_message(source)
        router.memory_service.remember("shared-rule " + marker, kind="constraint", layer="L1",
            source_refs=["message:" + source.id], related_quest_ids=[quest.id])
    router._sync_memory()
    result = router.memory_service.retrieve_context("shared-rule", project_id=projects[0][1]["id"])
    text = json.dumps(result)
    assert "ALPHA_PRIVATE" in text and "BETA_PRIVATE" not in text
    with store.connection() as c:
        snapshot = router._snapshot(c, "alpha_project progress")
    assert snapshot["project_context"]["focused_project_id"] == projects[0][1]["id"]
    assert {q["id"] for q in snapshot["quests"]} == {projects[0][0].id}


def test_focused_project_continuation_never_targets_other_project(rig):
    store, router, _triggers, projects = rig
    wrong = projects[1][0]
    router.provider = MockProvider(lambda *_: response(conversational_decision("continue_quest", quest_id=wrong.id)))
    result = asyncio.run(router.handle_user_message("Continue alpha_project work", request_id="wrong-project"))
    assert result["intent"] == "ambiguous" and result["quest_id"] is None


def test_project_selection_persists_without_becoming_tool_authority(rig):
    store, router, _triggers, projects = rig
    project = projects[0][1]
    router.provider = MockProvider(lambda *_: response({**conversational_decision(), "project_id": project["id"]}))
    result = asyncio.run(router.handle_user_message("New alpha_project analysis", request_id="new-alpha"))
    assert WorkspaceDiscovery(store).for_quest(result["quest_id"])["id"] == project["id"]
    assert WorkspaceDiscovery(store).associate_request(result["quest_id"])["id"] == project["id"]
    with store.connection() as c:
        assert c.execute("SELECT 1 FROM task_grants WHERE quest_id=?", (result["quest_id"],)).fetchone() is None


def test_long_context_compaction_keeps_project_chain(rig):
    store, router, _triggers, projects = rig
    for i in range(12):
        with store.unit_of_work() as work:
            work.add_message(ConversationMessage(role="user", content="background turn " + str(i)))
    ContextService(store).compact_router(keep_recent=2)
    with store.connection() as c:
        snapshot = router._snapshot(c, "alpha_project progress")

def _bounded_constraints(items, limit=10):
    seen, out = set(), []
    for item in items or []:
        if not isinstance(item, str):
            continue
        text = item.strip()
        if not text or len(text) > 500 or text in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(text)
        out.append(text)
        if len(out) >= limit:
            break
    return out


def _decision_error_digest(exc, limit=6):
    """Bounded, non-sensitive description of a rejected decision."""
    if isinstance(exc, ValidationError):
        items = []
        for error in exc.errors()[:limit]:
            location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
            items.append((location + ": " + str(error.get("msg", "")))[:180])
        return items or ["validation_failed"]
    return [str(exc)[:180]]

        )
        memory = self.memory_service.retrieve_context(
            text, quest_ids=explicit_ids, connection=connection, project_id=focused
        )
        # General recall may omit many matching constraint/message sources while
        # the actual Quest identity search is complete. Keep its finite search
        # separate; candidate-page omissions still make identity unresolved.
        quest_lookup = self.memory_service.retrieve_context(
            text,
            quest_ids=explicit_ids,
            kinds=("task",),
            source_types=("core_record",),
            limit=100,
            max_bytes=65536,
            connection=connection,
            project_id=focused,
        )
        recalled_ids = {
            quest_id
            for item in [*memory["items"], *quest_lookup["items"]]
            for quest_id in item["related_quest_ids"]
        }
        for quest_id in sorted(recalled_ids - included):
            quest = work.get_quest(quest_id)
            if quest and quest["conversation_id"] == "main":
                quests.append(quest)
                included.add(quest_id)
        events = work.list_events(after=state["event_cursor"], limit=200)
        evidence = [
            dict(row)
            for row in connection.execute(
                "SELECT id,quest_id,kind,trusted,payload,created_at FROM evidence ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 50"
            ).fetchall()
        ]
        models = [
            dict(row)
            for row in connection.execute(
                "SELECT id,profile,updated_at FROM models ORDER BY id LIMIT 100"
            ).fetchall()
        ]
        links = task_projects(connection, quests) if self.autonomous else {}
        return {
            "state": state,
            "quests": quests,
            "messages": messages,
            "context_capsule": capsule,
            "archive_head": self.context_service._router_archive_head(connection),
            "memory": memory,
            "quest_lookup": quest_lookup,
            "constraints": constraints,
            "recalled_ids": sorted(recalled_ids),
            "events": events,
            "evidence": evidence,
            "models": models,
            "quests_truncated": truncated,
            "completed_context": _completed_context(connection, quests) if self.autonomous else [],
            "project_context": project_focus,
            "task_projects": links,
            "coordination": coordination_context(connection, quests, links) if self.autonomous else [],
        }

    def _semantic_quests(self, connection, snapshot, recall):
        """Add only source-verified semantic task identities, preserving normal fencing."""
        ids = {
            quest_id
            for item in recall.get("items", [])
            if item.get("kind") == "task"
            for quest_id in item.get("related_quest_ids", [])
        }
        included = {quest["id"] for quest in snapshot["quests"]}
        for quest_id in sorted(ids - included):
            row = connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM quests WHERE id=? AND conversation_id='main'", (quest_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            if row:
                snapshot["quests"].append(dict(row))
        snapshot["recalled_ids"] = sorted(set(snapshot["recalled_ids"]) | ids)
        if self.autonomous:
            snapshot["completed_context"] = _completed_context(connection, snapshot["quests"])

    def _semantic_stable(self, connection, snapshot):
        for item in snapshot.get("semantic_memory", {}).get("items", []):
            current = self.memory_service.retrieve_context(
                "",
                source_refs=[item["id"]] if ":" in item["id"] else ["memory:" + item["id"]],
                limit=1,
                max_bytes=65536,
                connection=connection,
                exact_source_refs=True,
            )["items"]
            if not current or current[0] != item:
                return False
        return True

    def _context(self, snapshot, text):
        # UTF-8 byte count conservatively bounds byte-pair tokens; reserve output separately.
        effective_limit = self.context_limit
        profile = self._model_profile(snapshot)
        if profile is not None and profile.context_window:
            effective_limit = min(effective_limit, profile.context_window)
        if (
            profile is not None
            and profile.max_output_tokens is not None
            and self.output_reserve > profile.max_output_tokens
        ):
            raise DomainError("Router output reserve exceeds model maximum")
        compact = effective_limit < 65536
        schema_bytes = _decision_schema(compact=compact, autonomous=self.autonomous)
        instruction = schema_format_instruction(schema_bytes)
        read_tools = list(_READ_TOOLS)
        if self.autonomous:
            from .worker_superagent import RECALL_TOOL

            read_tools.append(RECALL_TOOL)

        def _overhead(policy):
            return (
                len(
                    _json({"tools": read_tools, "schema": schema_bytes, "policy": policy}).encode(
                        "utf-8"
                    )
                )
                + len(_json({"role": "system", "content": instruction}).encode("utf-8"))
                + 1024
            )

        # The detailed field contract is used when it leaves usable room; under a tight
        # budget the Router degrades to the short policy. The strict schema is never relaxed.
        policy = _POLICY_CORE if compact else _POLICY + " " + _POLICY_DETAIL
        if self.autonomous and not compact:
            policy += _AUTONOMOUS_DISPATCH_POLICY
        limit = effective_limit - self.output_reserve - _overhead(policy) - 512
        if not compact and limit - 4096 < 32768:
            # Under a tight window the Router keeps the short policy and spends the
            # budget on task state instead. The strict schema is never relaxed.
            policy = _POLICY
            limit = effective_limit - self.output_reserve - _overhead(policy) - 512
        if limit <= 0:
            raise DomainError("Router context budget exhausted")
        quest_summaries = [
            {
                "id": q["id"],
                "title": q["title"][:160],
                "goal": q["goal"][:160],
                "status": q["status"],
                "version": q["version"],
                "plan_revision": q["plan_revision"],
            }
            for q in snapshot["quests"]
        ]
        capsule = (
            _json(snapshot["context_capsule"])
            if snapshot["context_capsule"] is not None
            else snapshot["state"]["capsule"]
        )
        context = {
            "policy": policy,
            "identity": snapshot["state"]["router_session_id"],
            "capsule": capsule,
            "capsule_truncated": False,
            "quests": quest_summaries,
            "quests_truncated": snapshot["quests_truncated"],
            "recent_messages": [],
            "memory": [],
            "evidence": [],
            "events": [],
            "input": text,
        }
        if self.autonomous:
            context["project_context"] = snapshot["project_context"]
            context["coordination"] = snapshot["coordination"]
            context["recall"] = {
                "root": "conversation:main",
                "instruction": "Use recall_object with typed references (quest:, worker:, run:, thread:, trigger:, project:). "
                "Each recalled object includes next-hop references. Full contents remain externally stored.",
            }
            for quest in context["quests"]:
                quest["reference"] = "quest:" + quest["id"]
                quest["project_id"] = snapshot["task_projects"].get(quest["id"])
        if snapshot["constraints"]["items"]:
            context["constraints"] = snapshot["constraints"]
        explicit = set(re.findall(r"\bquest_[A-Za-z0-9]+\b", text)) | set(snapshot["recalled_ids"])
        # Context is itself JSON embedded in a provider message; reserve room for
        # escaping its quotes/backslashes and for the wire-format tool wrappers.
        content_limit = limit - 4096
        # A compacted archive capsule can outgrow a small window; bound it instead of
        # dropping the whole turn. The marker keeps the truncation visible to the model.
        context["capsule"], context["capsule_truncated"] = _bounded_capsule(
            context["capsule"], max(512, content_limit // 3)
        )
        while len(_json(context).encode("utf-8")) > content_limit:
            removable = next(
                (
                    index
                    for index in range(len(context["quests"]) - 1, -1, -1)
                    if context["quests"][index]["id"] not in explicit
                ),
                None,
            )
            if removable is None:
                break
            context["quests"].pop(removable)
            context["quests_truncated"] = True
        if len(_json(context).encode("utf-8")) > content_limit:
            raise DomainError("Router context budget exceeded")
        if self.autonomous:
            presented_quests = {quest["id"] for quest in context["quests"]}
            context["completed_context"] = []
            for item in snapshot["completed_context"]:
                if item["reference"][6:] not in presented_quests:
                    continue
                context["completed_context"].append(item)
                if len(_json(context).encode("utf-8")) > content_limit:
                    context["completed_context"].pop()
                    break
        cursor = snapshot["state"]["event_cursor"]
        for event in snapshot["events"]:
            context["events"].append(event)
            if len(_json(context).encode("utf-8")) > content_limit:
                context["events"].pop()
                break
            cursor = event["seq"]
        """Acknowledge routine autonomous facts without a Router model call."""

            "SELECT i.event_id FROM event_inbox i JOIN delegation_mandates m ON m.quest_id=i.quest_id "
            "WHERE i.consumer_id='router' AND m.state='active' AND i.processed_at IS NULL "
            "AND i.notice_dead_at IS NULL AND (i.notice_token IS NULL OR i.notice_next_attempt<=?) "
            "AND (i.event_type='worker.progress' OR (i.event_type='quest.status_changed' "
            "AND json_extract(i.payload,'$.to') IN ('approved','queued','running'))) "
            "ORDER BY i.seq LIMIT 100",
            (time.time(),),
        ).fetchall()
        for row in rows:
            connection.execute(
                "UPDATE event_inbox SET processed_at=?,notice_token=NULL WHERE consumer_id='router' "
                "AND event_id=? AND processed_at IS NULL",
                (now_iso(), row["event_id"]),
            )
        return len(rows)
